{{short description|Dutch-born mathematician and professor}}
'''Sigurd Bernardus Angenent''' (born 1960)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://viaf.org/viaf/284602381/ |title=Angenent, Sigurd Bernardus, 1960- |publisher=Virtual International Authority File |date= |accessdate=5 April 2016}}</ref> is a Dutch-born mathematician and was a professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] from 1987 until 2023. 

==Career==
Angenent was raised in [[Haarlem]], the [[Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/pictureofme.html |title=Personal page |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison |date= |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in Mathematics from [[Leiden University]] in 1986.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://discoveryportal.org/faculty.aspx?id=2510 |title=Researcher: Sigurd Angenent |publisher=Wisconsin Discovery Portal |date=20 February 2015 |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> He became professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1987.<ref name="prof">{{cite web|url=https://math.wisc.edu/staff/angenent-sigurd/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250718004830/https://math.wisc.edu/staff/angenent-sigurd/ |title=Sigurd Angenent |language=en |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison |date= |archive-date=18 July 2025}}</ref> In 1996 Angenent became a correspondent of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=knaw/> At the University of Wisconsin–Madison, he was the director of the Undergraduate Mathematics Program. After becoming frustrated with textbooks' high prices and poor quality, he wrote and made available his own notes for all classes.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://news.wisc.edu/22799 |title=Ten to receive Distinguished Teaching Awards |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison |date=1 May 2014 |accessdate=26 October 2020}}</ref> Angenent retired in 2023.<ref name="prof"/>

Angenent works on [[partial differential equation]]s and [[dynamical system]]s, with his recent research focusing on [[heat equation]] and [[diffusion equation]].<ref name=knaw>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/3802?set_language=en |title=Sigurd Angenent |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/ |title=Sigurd Angenent |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison |date= |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> The [[Angenent torus]] and [[Angenent oval]]s are special solutions to the [[mean curvature flow]] published by Angenent in 1992;<ref>{{citation
 | last = Angenent | first = Sigurd B.
 | contribution = Shrinking doughnuts
 | contribution-url = http://www.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/preprints/1989Gregynog/Gregynog.pdf
 | mr = 1167827
 | pages = 21–38
 | publisher = Birkhäuser | location = Boston, MA
 | series = Progress in Nonlinear Differential Equations and their Applications
 | title = Nonlinear diffusion equations and their equilibrium states, 3 (Gregynog, 1989)
 | volume = 7
 | year = 1992}}.</ref> The Angenent torus remains self-similar as it collapses to a point under the flow, and the Angenent ovals are the only compact convex [[ancient solution]]s other than [[circle]]s for the [[curve-shortening flow]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Daskalopoulos | first1 = Panagiota | author1-link = Panagiota Daskalopoulos
 | last2 = Hamilton | first2 = Richard | author2-link = Richard S. Hamilton
 | last3 = Sesum | first3 = Natasa | author3-link = Nataša Šešum
 | arxiv = 0806.1757
 | issue = 3
 | journal = Journal of Differential Geometry
 | mr = 2669361
 | pages = 455–464
 | title = Classification of compact ancient solutions to the curve shortening flow
 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jdg/1279114297
 | volume = 84
 | year = 2010| doi = 10.4310/jdg/1279114297 | bibcode = 2008arXiv0806.1757D| s2cid = 18747005 }}.</ref>
